limitations: Paused synthetic browser input and screenshot inspection; limited continuous human aiming and reaction assessment.

strengths: Strong cyan/amber rainy industrial identity, attractive title screen and clear terminal summary.
Memory receivers, floor rings, distance feedback and supply restoration establish a readable objective loop.
Precise optic aiming can remove wardens quickly; second attempt improved route time and accuracy.
issues: Boss aiming lanes are crowded by walls, pillars and low cover. I repeatedly saw components yet failed to damage them from my actual line of fire.
Boss exposure removed health rapidly while I was orienting and shooting. Paused input amplifies my aiming limits, but the transition felt much harsher than the recovery stage.
Enemy silhouettes and environments remain simple and repeated; visual polish does not reach modern AAA fidelity.
Compass shows fixed N/E labels around changing numeric headings, which I found less intuitive when making large turns.
assessment.enjoyment: Recovery navigation and deliberate optic shots were satisfying; boss obstruction and rapid damage frustrated me. Cannot substitute for sustained real time human play.

controls.aiming: Used right-button drag ADS sensitivity for turns, including large 940-1250 relative-x sweeps and small 40-95 corrections. Used screenshot positions to correct horizontal/vertical aim. Turn scale learned naturally; ADS narrows view. No privileged look controller.
